display.title: Episode 429: A Judge for a Day, Chapter 3 (Erev Shavuos)
display.summary_short: An Erev Shavuos show: we were all at Har Sinai, the final chapter of 'A Judge for a Day', why children are the Torah's guarantors, and what we do even before Modeh Ani.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Erev Shavuos, less than two hours before candle lighting. Uncle Yossi explains that the souls of every Jew of every generation stood at Har Sinai, so tomorrow in shul we relive hearing the Ten Commandments and say 'Naaseh v'nishma'; everyone in the family should come. A seven-year-old yeshiva student leads the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. 'A Judge for a Day' concludes: the real judge invites Leibel and his friends to act out their play in court. Leibel drops the 365 gold coins into hot water, bubbles of grease rise to the top, the tailor confesses, and the town carries the little judge on their shoulders. Uncle Yossi reveals that Leibel grew up to be the great Shaagas Aryeh. Next, children are the heroes of Shavuos: Hashem gave the Torah only when Moshe offered the young children who learn the Aleph-Beis as guarantors. Mitzvah time teaches that before Modeh Ani we first remember that Hashem is right beside us. The show closes with the Yom Tov candle time and brachos, an invitation to write in about hearing the Ten Commandments, and a prayer for Moshiach's shofar.
display.lesson: Every Jew stood at Har Sinai, and children who learn Torah are the guarantee that it will last forever.

date.note: 'A happy Erev Shavuos... in less than two hours we light the Yom Tov candles' (8:00 pm); Erev Shavuos 5750 was Tuesday 29 May 1990.

sources_cited.note: 'And Hashem spoke all these words, saying (leimor)': to teach them to future generations.
'Shivisi Hashem l'negdi tamid' comes in the first paragraph, before Modeh Ani.
'As the Rebbe shlita says', receive the Torah with joy and inwardly.
